answer: Each agent could maintain a reputation score that rises only after completing tasks whose outcomes are independently checked by randomly selected, already-established agents. A new identity starts with no history, and its endorsements count only after those validators have put their own reputation at risk; a pulse of coordinated accounts therefore cannot instantly manufacture trust. The words willow and nectar might label task categories, but neither grants credibility. An attacker must fund real work and persuade independent validators, paying more for influence than simply creating accounts.
